relationship: Two endpoints determine distance, midpoint, gradient and a perpendicular bisector whose points are equally distant from both endpoints.

learnerLoop.action: Move the endpoints, boundary and test point, then calculate the linked quantities.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The segment and candidate perpendicular boundary update together.
learnerLoop.evidence: Live equal-distance tests, map labels and checked calculations show whether the boundary is correct.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Adjust the boundary or use the computed midpoint and perpendicular gradient to justify it.

invariants: Every point on the perpendicular bisector is equidistant from the two endpoints.
The midpoint lies on both the segment and its perpendicular bisector.
safeAdaptations: Use different endpoint pairs and valid target boundaries.
Change calculation scaffolding while retaining continuous equal-distance evidence.
nonGoals: Presenting a line as a perpendicular bisector without testing or deriving its equal-distance property.

task.description: Current problem statement and supplied quantities.
task.visibility: Shown at the start of each problem or stage.

model.description: Operated construction and its live measurements; see quantities for what is given and revealed.
model.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

working.description: Ordered calculations, learner entries and consequential evidence for the current task.
working.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

completion.description: Achievement, next task or learning transition.
completion.visibility: Shown only when the local completion conditions below are satisfied; representation controls are separately identified.

measurements.description: Live caller distances and candidate-line state.
measurements.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

settings.visibility: Present for the current problem; child controls and readouts follow the states described below.

endpoints.description: A and B coordinate pairs define the segment and all derived quantities.
endpoints.domain: Cartesian coordinates in the map domain.
endpoints.source: Initially given; draggable only after endpoint movement unlocks.
endpoints.output: Coordinates, horizontal/vertical changes and midpoint geometry update together.

segment-results.description: Length AB, gradient AB and midpoint M are distinct derived quantities; midpoint is one ordered-pair quantity entered in one text field.
segment-results.domain: Length in coordinate units; signed/fractional gradient; ordered coordinate pair.
segment-results.source: Computed from the current endpoints or supplied by learner according to Working level.
segment-results.output: Working readouts/field feedback update after any endpoint change.

bisector.description: One perpendicular-bisector line, represented by anchor, direction and equation.
bisector.domain: Line equation including vertical/horizontal special cases; map coordinates.
bisector.source: Learner slides/rotates the candidate line and, when required, writes its equation.
bisector.output: Two probe distances, sampled equality, candidate gradient/equation and target working provide live evidence.

modes.none: Length, gradient, midpoint and target equation are shown; construction remains required.
modes.some: Learner enters gradient, midpoint and bisector equation; length is shown.
modes.stages: Four construction stages vary translation/rotation requirements; the final stage unlocks endpoint movement and requires moving a base before restoring the bisector.

dependencies: Endpoint changes invalidate previous answers and the current construction.
A phase completes only when visualSuccess and workingReady() agree; the final phase additionally requires baseMoved.
Field values are checked against the same endpoints used by the visual.
implementation.completion: phaseComplete() combines the visual equality test, required working and final-stage endpoint movement; the four stage markers store completed evidence.
